relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a girl with Blau syndrome: "She had been diagnosed with BS when she was 19 months old."
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON. One in-scope person (the single unnamed case-report patient, label 'patient'), in scope by diagnosis of Blau syndrome. The paper reports no genetic testing and prints no NOD2 variant for her, and does not tie a NOD2 variant to her, so the variants table is empty; n_patients_reported (patients with a NOD2 variant) is left null. Clinical diagnosis basis for BS is not stated. Age at last evaluation is not stated (six-year-old at referral, followed up 6 months later), so left not reported; the age at referral is the span of the label. Checklist: 'visual impairment or blindness' marked observed from reduced BCVA 20/70 and 20/80 plus blurry vision (judgement call; the paper does not use the word impairment for her). Retinal vasculitis was recorded as a phenotypic feature but the vasculitis checklist item (large-vessel, aortitis, leukocytoclastic) was left not reported because retinal vasculitis is not one of the listed types. Intraocular pressures (17/18, 20/21, 19 mm Hg) are given without being called normal or raised, so glaucoma/raised IOP is not reported. Macular OCT 'normal structure and contour' is a normal investigation as a whole; recorded as written (abnormal macular structure and contour, excluded) and nothing more specific was excluded. Aseptic meningitis is recorded as a reported event (attributed to cyclophosphamide) rather than a disease feature. Paper inconsistency: the drug is called fluocinolone acetonide 0.19 mg throughout but 'triamcinolone acetonide 0.19 mg' / 'triamcinolone' in the Discussion; treatment summary follows the case report wording. Supplementary material is only the CARE checklist (not included in the text).

treatment_summary.value: Topical cycloplegics and corticosteroids OU; systemic mycophenolate mofetil 250 mg twice a day, tofacitinib 4 mg daily, prednisone 9 mg daily and infliximab 10 mg/kg monthly; previously failed naproxen, methotrexate, etanercept, tocilizumab, canakinumab, rilonacept, anakinra, golimumab and intravenous immunoglobulin; cyclophosphamide pulse therapy stopped due to aseptic meningitis; intravitreal fluocinolone acetonide 0.19 mg implant in both eyes, after which topical cycloplegic and corticosteroid treatments were discontinued.
span: She was on frequent topical cycloplegics and corticosteroids in both eyes for her uveitis. Systemically, she was taking mycophenolate mofetil 250 mg twice a day, tofacitinib 4 mg daily, and prednisone 9 mg daily. Additionally, she was receiving infliximab at a dose of 10 mg/kg monthly.

She had already failed naproxen, methotrexate, etanercept, tocilizumab, canakinumab, rilonacept, anakinra, golimumab, and intravenous immunoglobulin because of their ineffectiveness or adverse effects.
She had also received cyclophosphamide pulse therapy which had been stopped due to aseptic meningitis.
we decided to proceed with intravitreal fluocinolone acetonide 0.19 mg implant implantation OU
These medications were discontinued after intravitreal triamcinolone implant implantation.
